name: X-FAB Sarawak fab, Kuching (2025 cleanroom expansion)

process_nodes.label: 180nm BCD-on-SOI (XT018)
process_nodes.note: The expansion more than doubles capacity for this platform, which supports 10 V to 375 V devices.

summary: X-FAB's wafer fab in Kuching, Sarawak, which gained 6,000 square metres of cleanroom in an expansion opened in September 2025 by Malaysia's Prime Minister and the Sarawak Premier. X-FAB put the expansion at $600 million and Malaysia's investment agency at RM3 billion; it took about two years from groundbreaking to the first production lots. The new line more than doubles capacity for X-FAB's 180nm BCD-on-SOI platform, used for motor and LED drivers, battery management and medical ultrasound chips, and raised the fab's monthly wafer starts from 30,000 to 40,000.

metrics.note: Stated with a dollar sign only; X-FAB reports in US dollars.
The Malaysian investment agency's figure for the same expansion.
Monthly wafer starts for the whole Sarawak fab after the expansion, up from 30,000; wafer size not stated.

milestones.note: Opening ceremony for the new manufacturing line, which had already run its first production lots.

sources.title: X-FAB Opens New Cleanroom at its Malaysian Site
X-FAB's RM3 Billion State-of-the-Art Expansion in Sarawak Strengthens Malaysia's Position as Global Semiconductor Hub

notes: The record covers the whole Sarawak fab, with the 2025 cleanroom as a phase: the investment and cleanroom area apply to the expansion, while the 40,000 wafer-start figure covers the whole fab. The release does not give the groundbreaking date or the wafer size.

review.method: Independent AI-assisted review (Claude): re-opened every cited source, checked each statement against it and searched for newer reporting.
review.changes: Rescoped the record to the Sarawak fab with the 2025 cleanroom as a phase, so the site-wide 40,000 wafer-start capacity applies to the facility instead of being marked multi-site, and the investment, cleanroom area and opening apply to the expansion phase; added the Malaysian Investment Development Authority release with its RM3 billion figure.
